page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a woodcut initial opens the Concio paragraph; a centred heading with a verse reference; no marginal notes; signature at the foot.

main_text.p: tale proferre. In vobis ergo omnis culpa hæret, nec repudiatis vxoribus, sed turpissimæ adulteræ similes estis, quæ marito relicto amatores suos sectatur, &c. Quoad ergo consilium siue priuilegium per Mosem datum, ista repudiorum ratio mala non erat: merito autem reprehendi debebant Iudæi, qui hanc in effrenem suæ libidinis licentiam conuerterant: quæ causa est, quod illos Dominus nunc arctioribus terminis constringit.

Habemus in his exemplum memorabile, quæ optima sit in legibus ciuilibus dispen-sandi ratio, & quando illa admitti, quando item legum authoritas seuerius vrgeri ac retineri debeat. Christus Iesus Dominus & seruator noster det nobis intellectum in omnibus, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XLVI
Matth. 19. -
main_text.p: DICVNT ei discipuli eius: Si ad ipsum modum habet causa hominis cum uxore[?], non expedit contrahere matrimonium. Qui dixit illis: Non omnes capaces sunt huius dicti, sed quibus datum est. Sunt enim eunuchi, qui de matris utero sic nati sunt: & sunt eunuchi, qui facti sunt eunuchi ab hominibus: & sunt

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated D set in a framed box; the first word is DICVNT with the initial D from the woodcut. The line "uxore" is followed by a curved mark that I could not identify with certainty, so I read it as a stop-like sign with [?]. The page number "195" is a long, italic-style numeral; the final digit is doubtful. The running head "NVPTIALES." has a decorated initial N and the V in place of U is kept as printed. The signature "T 4" stands at the foot. The text breaks off mid-sentence at the end of the page ("& sunt"), which continues on the next page.
